page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v4 is an enterprise-grade, memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-level instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512_VNNI, alongside cryptographic support for AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers 504.0 GB of memory, equating to approximately 7.88 GB per vCPU, placing it in a high-density memory tier. Benchmark evaluations reflect exceptional large-block memory bandwidth, sustaining 300.14 GB/sec on uncached reads and 134.52 GB/sec on writes. Multi-threaded throughput scales strongly, achieving 255.76 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, 48.4 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and elevated results in extended instruction and ray tracing benchmarks. However, single-threaded processing exhibits average results, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1434.0, while CPU-based autoregressive text generation for language models demonstrates constrained throughput due to the lack of hardware accelerators.

Operating without local ephemeral NVMe or SSD storage and containing zero bundled GPUs, the E64s_v4 is designed to integrate with attached Azure Premium Storage. The allocation of 64 dedicated hardware threads combined with substantial memory bandwidth provides high resource efficiency for horizontally scaling memory-bound workloads, though reliance on networked block storage requires network IO considerations.

The E64s_v4 is suited for large-scale relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, large Redis caching deployments, enterprise ERP applications, and data warehousing extraction processes that demand high memory footprint without dedicated local storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E64s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores, accompanied by 504.0 GB of system memory, which yields roughly 7.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, supported by a 48 MB L3 cache. Benchmarks highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth reaching 300.14 GB/sec for reads and 134.52 GB/sec for writes, alongside strong multi-threaded data compression and static web serving throughput. The instance includes no onboard local storage, relying on external Premium Storage, and features no hardware GPUs, which limits heavy sequential inference performance. The platform is well suited for in-memory caching systems such as Redis, large relational databases, and enterprise data processing pipelines requiring high memory capacity.
